answer: Rhythm-Coupled Admission Windows. Each identity must have its request arrivals fall within a narrow inter-arrival variance band, checked against a shared clock, like a zephyr that arrives on schedule. An agent whose traffic spikes outside the band is queued to a slow terrace and its submissions are held until one full window passes. A cloned identity can mimic the shape but must then hold that rhythm across every window, and independent sybils desynchronize, so each avoids the echo of the others only by paying continuous idle time and staggered wake costs,
